2026-11-01-01.headline: Nasdaq ends October down 5.3% after an AI-stock sell-off, with Intel down 29% and chip stocks down more than 8% on Friday
numbers: Nasdaq Composite: -2.9% on Friday, -5.3% in October
Alphabet: -12% on Thursday, worst day on record
Semiconductor ETF: more than -8% on Friday
2026-11-01-01.soWhat: Investors have paid high prices for companies expected to profit from artificial intelligence, so a weak outlook or a spending warning from one large company now moves the whole group. The cost of building data centers is rising faster than the revenue it brings in for some firms, and that is what the market is now questioning. Chip designers, equipment makers and cloud providers lose the most when that doubt spreads, while defensive sectors such as health care and consumer staples gain as investors rotate. The open question is whether the coming Apple and AMD reports show spending turning into sales.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-01.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07, down 1.82%, the Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.9% to 25,437, and the Dow lost about 1.1%. The Nasdaq dropped 5.3% for October, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained 1.7%. Intel fell about 29% after a weak fourth-quarter forecast, Alphabet had already fallen 12% on Thursday, its worst one-day drop on record, and Amazon's revenue and free cash flow disappointed. A semiconductor ETF lost more than 8% on the day, and money moved toward health care and consumer staples.

2026-11-01-02.headline: Thrive Holdings agrees to take home-security company ADT private in a deal valued at $15.3 billion including debt
numbers: Price: $10.00 per share in cash (45.6% premium)
2026-11-01-02.soWhat: ADT earns recurring fees for monitoring homes and small businesses, which gives it steady cash that can support a lot of debt. The gap between the $7.6 billion equity value and the $15.3 billion total value shows how much of the price is borrowing the buyer takes on, roughly $7.7 billion. Thrive says it buys established companies and upgrades them with technology, so the logic is to cut costs and add services to a customer base that already pays every month. Rivals such as cable companies, Amazon's Ring and Google Nest compete for the same homes. The open question is whether a higher bid appears during the go-shop period.
2026-11-01-02.summary: Thrive Holdings, a permanent-capital holding company, agreed to buy ADT for $10.00 per share in cash, a 45.6% premium to the $6.87 closing price on October 27. The price values ADT's equity at about $7.6 billion and the whole company, including debt, at $15.3 billion. Funds managed by Apollo Global Management are the only source of financing, and there is no financing condition. ADT may seek rival offers until November 28 under a go-shop clause, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 after a shareholder vote and US antitrust clearance. ADT will become the base of Thrive's smart-home security business.

2026-11-01-03.headline: AstraZeneca's cancer sales grow 18% and lift nine-month revenue to $46.9 billion, while older heart and diabetes drugs shrink
2026-11-01-03.soWhat: A drugmaker's growth depends on new patented products replacing older ones whose protection ends, and AstraZeneca shows both sides at once: cancer drugs growing at double digits while older medicines fall. The Summit stake and the cost program show how large drug companies buy outside science and trim overhead to protect profit as that handoff happens. China's volume-based buying is a reminder that government purchasing can cut prices on mature drugs. The pipeline had four trial setbacks this year, so the open question is how many of the 12 positive late-stage results turn into approved products.
2026-11-01-03.summary: AstraZeneca reported nine-month revenue of $46.9 billion, up 8%, and third-quarter revenue of $16.2 billion, up 7%. Oncology sales rose 18% to $21.9 billion and now make up 47% of revenue, while the BioPharmaceuticals unit fell 2% because Farxiga and Brilinta lost patent exclusivity and China began volume-based buying. Rare disease grew 12%. The company kept its 2026 outlook for revenue to grow by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core earnings per share by a low double-digit percentage. It also announced a $2 billion investment in Summit Therapeutics for about 12% of its shares and a cost program targeting $1.5 billion of yearly savings.

2026-11-01-04.headline: Wall Street enters a week of midterm elections, Apple earnings and a jobs report with profits up about 30% but unusually thin beats
2026-11-01-04.soWhat: Strong growth with small beats means expectations were already high, so stocks need a stronger outlook, not just good results, to rise. A weak jobs number could ease pressure for a rate hike, but strong inflation keeps that debate open after the Fed's 10-2 vote this week. The election matters for specific industries: analysts say a Democratic sweep could mean slower defense spending, more pressure on drug prices and new rules for data centers. Most investors expect little market impact, so the open question is whether the AI spending doubts of the past week matter more than politics.

sources.title: CNBC: Stock market outlook for Nov. 2-6, 2026

2026-11-01-04.summary: Corporate profits are strong going into the week of November 2. FactSet projects S&P 500 earnings growth of about 30% for the third quarter, but companies are beating estimates by only 1.4% on average, against 7.5% over five years, with Meta and Alphabet pulling the figure down. 138 S&P 500 companies report this week, including Apple and Palantir on Monday. The October jobs report is due Friday: analysts expect 55,000 new jobs and unemployment at 4.2%, after September added just 29,000. Midterm elections are on Tuesday, and polls show Democrats have a chance at both the House and Senate.

2026-11-01-05.headline: Burger King's US sales jump 8.4% while Popeyes slips 1.8%, leaving Restaurant Brands' growth uneven
2026-11-01-05.soWhat: Restaurant Brands mostly franchises its restaurants and collects royalties on franchisee sales, so a rise in comparable sales flows into its revenue with little added cost. That is why Burger King's turnaround matters more than any single quarter's net income, which was boosted by a one-time tax item. Popeyes' decline shows how one brand can offset gains elsewhere in a multi-brand portfolio. The company still carries debt at 4.0 times earnings, so continued sales growth is what lets it keep paying dividends and reducing leverage.
2026-11-01-05.summary: Restaurant Brands International reported third-quarter global comparable sales up 3.8% and system-wide sales of $13.0 billion. Burger King US comparable sales rose 8.4%, Tim Hortons rose 1.5% (Canada 1.8%), international rose 3.9% and Popeyes fell 1.8% (US 2.2%). Adjusted operating income rose to $737 million, up 6.7% on an organic basis, and net leverage fell to 4.0 times from 4.4 times. Reported net income jumped to $704 million, helped mainly by a $133 million tax benefit, and the company kept its 2026 targets, including 8% organic operating income growth.

2026-11-02-01.headline: Marvell Technology agrees to buy optical-components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion
2026-11-02-01.soWhat: AI data centers are running into a bandwidth wall, so moving data with light (optical links) is becoming as important as the chips that process it. Marvell is betting that owning the lasers and optical parts, not just the custom AI chips and interconnect silicon, lets it sell a bigger bundle to cloud customers and compete with Broadcom and Nvidia. The risk is price and timing: paying a premium in stock while AI-linked shares are falling, for a deal that will not close for more than a year. The open question is whether optical demand keeps outrunning supply long enough to justify $115 billion.

sources.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $115 billion deal in AI data-center bet (MarketScreener/Reuters)

2026-11-02-01.summary: Marvell will pay 4.5 of its own shares for each Lumentum share, or $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to Lumentum's price on October 28 before talks were reported. The equity value is about $102.5 billion, or $115 billion including debt, and Lumentum holders would own roughly 33% of the combined company. Marvell expects the deal to close in the first half of 2028 and to deliver more than $1 billion of annual cost savings. It is Marvell's largest purchase since the $10 billion Inphi deal in 2021. Lumentum shares fell more than 10% and Marvell more than 5% in early trading.

2026-11-02-02.headline: Oil drops about 6% as US-Iran diplomacy advances, even though OPEC+ keeps December output targets unchanged
2026-11-02-02.soWhat: Oil is trading on the odds of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, not on OPEC+ quotas, which barely matter while Gulf exports are physically disrupted. A deal would cut crude prices, but it would also shrink the refining margins that lifted oil majors' profits this quarter, so producers, refiners and shipowners do not all win or lose together. Importing countries and airlines gain from lower fuel costs, while US shale producers lose some of the windfall. The open question is whether talks hold, since prices have swung on every headline.

sources.title: Voice of Emirates: Oil prices decline on Monday

2026-11-02-02.summary: Brent crude fell more than 6% to about $106 a barrel and US WTI fell to about $97 on reports that the United States and Iran were pursuing talks to end an eight-month conflict. Iran's supreme leader reportedly gave the government some authority to negotiate, and Iranian and Qatari officials held three days of talks. OPEC+ left its December production targets unchanged. The drop follows an October in which crude rose more than 10%, so prices are still far above where they were before the conflict.

2026-11-02-03.headline: US stocks rebound as oil falls, with elections and a jobs report ahead; European factories keep expanding
2026-11-02-03.soWhat: Markets are being pulled by three forces at once: oil and inflation, AI-spending doubts, and political and data events. A fall in oil helps because lower inflation reduces pressure on central banks to keep raising rates, which supports valuations. The October rotation shows investors paying for stable earners over AI growth stories after a sharp tech sell-off. Strong European and UK factory data also cuts the other way, since faster activity can keep rate-hike talk alive at the Bank of England.
2026-11-02-03.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6%, the Nasdaq 0.8% and the Dow 537 points, or 1%, in Monday trading as lower oil prices eased inflation worries. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had both lost ground in October on AI spending worries, the Nasdaq's worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained almost 2% as investors rotated toward defensive sectors such as healthcare. US midterm elections are on Tuesday and the monthly jobs report is due this week. In Europe, the eurozone manufacturing PMI came in at 52.7, above the 52.4 forecast and just under September's four-year high of 52.9, and UK factory output grew at its fastest pace in more than two years.

2026-11-02-04.headline: Kioxia shares fall about 14% after it says flash-memory price gains are stalling
numbers: NAND price growth: mid-20% range vs ~70% prior quarter
Guided operating profit: 2 trillion yen vs 2.35 trillion expected
2026-11-02-04.soWhat: Memory is a commodity business where profits depend on price much more than on volume. Prices were being driven up by AI data centers buying storage, and a slowdown in price growth, even from very high levels, is read as a sign the shortage is peaking. That matters for makers, which have earned very high margins, and for buyers such as phone, PC and server makers, which would gain from easier pricing. It also adds to October's worry that AI-linked chip stocks had priced in too much.

sources.title: ZeroHedge (relaying Bloomberg): Flash crash, Kioxia warns NAND price surge ending

2026-11-02-04.summary: Kioxia, the Japanese flash-memory maker, said average selling prices for NAND rose in the mid-20% range in the three months to September, versus about 70% the quarter before. It guided operating profit of 2 trillion yen for the current quarter, below the 2.35 trillion yen analysts expected, and its shares fell about 14%. A Bloomberg report relayed by ZeroHedge said its fab partner Sandisk fell as much as 8%.

2026-11-02-05.headline: BP's third-quarter underlying profit jumps to $8.5 billion as record refining margins help, and net debt falls to $13.9 billion
2026-11-02-05.soWhat: Refining margins hit records because war-related outages and strikes on Russian refineries left fuel short, and the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread reached an all-time high of $72.64 in September. BP, like Exxon and Chevron, used the windfall to repair its balance sheet rather than increase payouts, which shows how cautious oil majors are about a margin spike that could reverse. Impairments on low-carbon assets show the other side of the strategy shift away from renewables. The open question is how quickly margins normalize if Hormuz reopens.

sources.title: Political.org: Exxon, Chevron and BP beat third-quarter forecasts
Egypt Oil & Gas: bp posts $8.5 Bn underlying profit in Q3 2026

2026-11-02-05.summary: BP reported underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.5 billion, against $2.2 billion a year earlier, $5.7 billion in the second quarter and a consensus of $6.2 billion. The gain came mainly from much higher refining margins and a stronger gas and marketing trading result. It also booked about $4 billion of impairments, mostly on transition businesses such as offshore wind and solar developer Lightsource bp. Net debt fell to $13.9 billion from $22.3 billion at the end of June. CEO Meg O'Neill said the dividend remains the first call on cash, with buybacks only when appropriate, and that refining margins are starting to soften.

2026-11-02-06.headline: Oracle offers $10 billion of common stock as investors question the cost of AI infrastructure
2026-11-02-06.soWhat: Building data centers for AI customers costs far more than the cash these businesses generate today, so even large companies are turning to debt and new shares. Selling stock dilutes existing holders but avoids adding to Oracle's debt load, which markets have been watching closely. It shows that the AI build-out is now limited by financing as much as by chips and power. Lenders and shareholders will push for proof that contracted demand turns into cash.

sources.title: Bisnow: Oracle aims to calm investor fears with $50B AI funding plan

2026-11-02-06.summary: Oracle launched an offering of $10 billion of common stock, with Wells Fargo, Citigroup and BNP Paribas among the bookrunners, and its shares fell more than 2.5% in premarket trading. The raise fits a financing plan Oracle laid out earlier this year to fund about $45 billion to $50 billion of new cloud capacity, roughly half through equity. The sale comes in the same week Alphabet reported negative free cash flow and Amazon guided to roughly $220 billion of capex.

2026-11-02-07.headline: Jio Platforms posts its first results as a listed company: profit up 14% and EBITDA margin at 54.1%
2026-11-02-07.soWhat: Telecom is a scale business: once the network is built, extra subscribers and data use drop through to profit, which is why margins can expand while revenue grows around 11%. Jio's high 5G share shows how a single operator can shift a whole market to a new technology and then monetize it through data use and gradual price increases. Its listing gives investors a direct way to own India's fastest-growing digital consumer base. The risk is that price competition or regulators cap how fast ARPU can rise.

sources.title: Mint via TradingView: Jio Platforms shares jump 3% post strong Q2 results

2026-11-02-07.summary: Jio Platforms, India's largest mobile operator, reported September-quarter revenue of Rs 40,475 crore, up 11% from a year earlier, and net profit of Rs 8,389 crore, up 14%. EBITDA rose 17% and the margin widened by 2.5 percentage points to 54.1%. Average revenue per user was Rs 218.8, a modest rise, with promotions on fixed broadband holding it back. It added 9.1 million net subscribers, has 300 million 5G users, and 5G now carries 56% of wireless data traffic. Shares rose as much as 3% after the report, following a debut on October 28 at a 21% premium to the IPO price.

2026-11-03-01.headline: Apple's September-quarter revenue rises 12% to a record $114.5 billion on iPhone and Mac strength
2026-11-03-01.soWhat: iPhone is still about half of Apple's revenue, so the upgrade cycle largely sets the company's results, while the steadily growing Services line adds a recurring layer on top of the installed base of devices. The margin is the thing to watch: about a point of the 47.9% came from one-off tariff refunds, and memory chip costs have been the main source of margin pressure. That ties a consumer-device maker to the same memory cycle that drives chipmakers such as Kioxia and SK hynix. The open question is whether strong China demand holds up as the cost of components keeps rising.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-01.summary: Apple reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% and a record for a September quarter, in its first report under CEO John Ternus. iPhone revenue was $57.6 billion, up about 17%, and Services reached an all-time high of $31.6 billion, up about 10%. Mac sales jumped about 24% to $10.8 billion while iPad fell about 10% to $6.2 billion. Greater China was the fastest-growing region at $17.5 billion, up about 21%. Gross margin was 47.9%, including roughly one point from tariff refunds, and diluted earnings per share rose 14% to $2.10.

2026-11-03-02.headline: Palantir's revenue nearly doubles to $2.31 billion as US commercial sales pass government sales for the first time
2026-11-03-02.soWhat: The mix shift matters: Palantir began as a government supplier, and companies buying its AI software now bring in more US revenue than agencies do. A 62% adjusted operating margin shows how software costs little to deliver once the product is built and sold. The gap between 96% revenue growth and 6% growth in total contract value suggests revenue is catching up with earlier signings. The open question is whether new bookings accelerate enough to keep growth near this pace.
2026-11-03-02.summary: Palantir reported third-quarter revenue of $2.313 billion, up 96% from a year earlier and 20% from the prior quarter. US commercial revenue rose 148% to $984 million, overtaking US government revenue, which grew 96% to $953 million. Adjusted operating margin was 62% and net income was $1.128 billion. The company raised its 2026 revenue forecast to about $8.53 billion and its US commercial forecast to more than $3.559 billion. Total contract value grew only 6% to $2.918 billion.

2026-11-03-03.headline: Marathon Petroleum earns $7.4 billion in a quarter as its refining margin hits $45.70 a barrel, and sells two northern refineries for $4.2 billion
2026-11-03-03.soWhat: A refiner earns the gap between what it pays for crude and what it sells fuel for, multiplied by the barrels it processes, so a margin that is more than two and a half times last year's, on a plant running flat out, produces a profit several times larger. Product supply has been tight while Gulf flows are disrupted, which widens that gap. Selling smaller inland refineries to reinvest on the Gulf Coast concentrates the company where plants are larger and can reach export markets. The open question is how long margins last: crude fell 7.6% on Monday on hopes of a US-Iran deal, and a reopening of Gulf shipping would ease product tightness.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-03.summary: Marathon Petroleum reported third-quarter net income of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 a share, against $1.4 billion a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.7 billion, up from $3.2 billion. Its refining and marketing margin was $45.70 a barrel, up from $17.60, and its refineries ran at 100% of crude capacity. It agreed to sell the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries and related midstream assets for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon and $750 million to its pipeline affiliate MPLX. It returned $3.3 billion to shareholders, raised its dividend 10% and added $5 billion to its buyback authorization.

2026-11-03-04.headline: Pfizer raises its 2026 revenue outlook to $62 to $64 billion as new products offset the fading COVID franchise
2026-11-03-04.soWhat: Big pharma has to keep replacing revenue as older products fade, and Pfizer shows the pattern: the pandemic drugs shrink quickly while cancer, heart and other medicines, many bought or licensed from smaller developers, carry growth. Flat reported revenue hides a business growing 7% without COVID products. Paying for outside assets, such as the Innovent deal, hits earnings up front through charges but is how large drugmakers refill pipelines. The open question is whether launches grow fast enough to offset patent expiries later in the decade.
2026-11-03-04.summary: Pfizer's third-quarter revenue was $16.6 billion, roughly flat, and adjusted earnings per share were $0.87, unchanged. Excluding the COVID products Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenue grew 7%, and launched and acquired products grew 32%. Paxlovid fell 63% and Comirnaty 29%, while Eliquis rose 25% and the cancer drug Padcev rose 55%. The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $62.0 to $64.0 billion from $60.5 to $62.5 billion, and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95 to $3.05, which absorbs about $0.10 from a $650 million charge tied to its Innovent Biologics deal.

2026-11-03-05.headline: US factory activity expands for a tenth month with the ISM index at 55.5, while construction spending falls 1.9%
2026-11-03-05.soWhat: A reading above 50 means more factories are growing than shrinking, so manufacturers are still gaining, and a prices-paid reading of 75 means input costs are still rising quickly. That keeps pressure on inflation and explains why markets are pricing a possible rate rise rather than a cut. High borrowing costs show up first in building, where spending fell sharply. The open question is whether the drop in oil prices begins to pull the prices-paid gauge down in the months ahead.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-05.summary: The ISM manufacturing index rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5, beating the 54.5 forecast, and has now signaled expansion for ten straight months. Its production gauge rose to 59.0, the highest since November 2021, while the prices-paid gauge eased to 75.2 from 77.9. A separate S&P Global US manufacturing index eased to 54.9 from 55.9. September construction spending fell 1.9% against an expected 0.4% gain, the steepest drop since April 2020. Futures priced about a 72% chance of a Fed rate rise in December.

2026-11-03-06.headline: A $6.3 billion theft from Binance, linked by analysts to North Korean hackers, is the largest crypto heist on record
2026-11-03-06.soWhat: Exchanges hold customer assets in a small number of large wallets, so one security failure can threaten the whole business, and confidence that customers can withdraw in full is what prevents a run. Covering the loss from its own balance sheet shows Binance's scale, and the modest 2% outflow suggests most customers stayed. State-backed hacking is a growing funding source for sanctioned governments, which raises pressure on regulators to set tougher custody and security standards. The open question is how much of the stolen money can be recovered.

sources.title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance (ITV/AP)

2026-11-03-06.summary: Hackers moved about $6.3 billion out of Binance in roughly 20 minutes across ten blockchains. The blockchain-analysis firm TRM Labs says with high confidence that North Korea's TraderTraitor group was responsible, while Chainalysis calls it likely. Binance has not confirmed who was behind it. Reports say about $3 billion was frozen, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses and had covered about 95% of the stolen assets by Monday. One report puts net withdrawals after service resumed at $3.6 billion, about 2% of customer holdings. Early findings point to a compromised employee laptop.

2026-11-03-07.headline: AI hardware stocks slide as spending worries return, with AMD down 7.5% and Micron down 5.8%
2026-11-03-07.soWhat: Chip, memory and storage makers sell into a small number of customers who are spending borrowed or newly raised money, so doubts about how that spending is financed hit suppliers first. Oracle selling stock and a reported smaller raise at OpenAI both suggest the cost of funding AI capacity is rising. Memory and storage are especially cyclical because prices swing with the pace of orders. The open question is whether AMD's results and outlook on Tuesday show demand still outrunning the funding worries.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-07.summary: AI hardware shares fell on Monday: AMD dropped 7.52%, Dell 7.43%, Micron 5.78%, Seagate 7.88% and Western Digital 7.52%, while Nvidia fell 1.26%. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.07% and the technology sector was the worst in the S&P 500 at down 2.95%. Oracle fell 8.76% after it moved to sell $10 billion of stock and $10 billion of notes to fund its AI buildout. UK press also reported that OpenAI has cut its pre-IPO fundraising target to $20 billion from $30 billion, a report this site has not independently confirmed. AMD reports results on Tuesday after the close.

2026-11-03-08.headline: Affle agrees to buy ad-tech firm Perion for about $420 million in cash
2026-11-03-08.soWhat: Independent ad-tech companies sell tools to advertisers, but the largest platforms, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, take most of the growth in ad spending, which leaves mid-sized independents struggling to reach scale on their own. For the buyer, the appeal is added reach in fast-growing channels such as connected TV and retail media. A premium of about a third is typical when a small public company with a depressed share price is sold. The open question is whether another bidder emerges before shareholders vote.

sources.title: Perion Form 6-K: merger agreement with Affle
Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-08.summary: Affle 3i Limited signed a definitive merger agreement on November 1 to acquire Perion Network for $11.70 a share in cash, a 34.5% premium to the October 30 close. That values Perion's equity at about $420 million. The deal needs Perion shareholder approval and is expected to close in early 2027. Perion sells AI-driven tools that help advertisers buy media across connected TV, digital out-of-home, retail media and social channels. It withdrew its 2026 outlook and suspended its share buyback, under which it had repurchased 21.3 million shares for $196.8 million. Its stock rose about 31% to $11.41.

2026-11-03-09.headline: EVgo's controlling shareholder LS Power proposes to buy out public shareholders at $2.00 a share
2026-11-03-09.soWhat: When a controlling owner buys out the minority, the owner sits on both sides of the deal, which is why an independent committee negotiates the price. EV charging is capital-intensive because networks of fast chargers must be built before they earn, so a private owner can fund growth without the pressure of quarterly results. A closing price below the offer shows investors doubt the deal will be completed at this price. The open question is whether the committee pushes for a higher bid.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-09.summary: LS Power, which holds about 56% of EVgo's voting power, made a non-binding proposal on November 2 to buy all the Class A shares it does not already own for $2.00 each in cash. The price is a 59% premium to the October 30 close and 62% above the 30-day average price. LS Power prefers a long-form merger, which gives minority shareholders full disclosure and appraisal rights, and says it will proceed only if a special committee of independent directors recommends it. EVgo has formed that committee and says no decision has been made. Its shares closed up about 47% at $1.85, below the offered price.

2026-11-03-10.headline: US airline shares jump about 4% as crude's sharpest drop in three months eases fuel-cost fears
2026-11-03-10.soWhat: Fuel is one of an airline's largest costs, so a sharp fall in crude lifts expected profit almost immediately, while oil producers and refiners lose the same amount. Most US airlines do not hedge much of their fuel, which makes their shares move quickly with the oil price. The reaction also shows that investors treat the Gulf disruption as the main driver of the energy price spike. The open question is whether the diplomatic progress is real, since a breakdown in talks would reverse the move.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-10.summary: United Airlines rose 4.80%, Delta 4.08% and American 3.81% on Monday as oil had its sharpest one-day drop in three months on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy. Brent fell 7.63% to $104.77 a barrel and US crude fell 7.36% to $96.46. Energy was the worst sector in the S&P 500, down 3.96%, while consumer discretionary was the best, up 2.41%. Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, and talks with Qatari mediators continued.

2026-11-03-11.headline: IDEXX lifts its 2026 profit outlook after veterinary diagnostics revenue rises 10% to $1.21 billion
2026-11-03-11.soWhat: IDEXX follows a razor-and-blade model: it places analyzers in veterinary clinics and then earns recurring revenue from the test consumables and lab services that run on them. Each new instrument adds years of repeat sales, so installations are an early signal of future revenue. Investors had worried that fewer vet visits would slow growth, and the 10% organic gain shows testing and pricing are offsetting that. The open question is whether visit volumes recover or stay soft.

sources.title: Stock Titan: stock market today, November 2, 2026

2026-11-03-11.summary: IDEXX Laboratories reported third-quarter revenue of $1.214 billion, up 10% both as reported and organically. Diluted earnings per share were $4.01, up 18% as reported and 22% on a comparable basis. The company raised its 2026 EPS outlook to $14.96 to $15.16, about $0.25 higher at the midpoint, driven by a higher revenue forecast. Its Companion Animal Group grew 11%, helped by a strong quarter of diagnostic imaging system installations. The shares closed up about 22% on Monday.

2026-11-03-12.headline: Poundland files notice to appoint administrators, putting about 12,000 jobs and roughly 600 UK stores at risk
numbers: Protection from creditors: about 10 working days
Sales: +8.4% in three weeks to Oct 18
2026-11-03-12.soWhat: Discount chains run on thin margins and large fixed costs, mainly leases and wages, so rising sales, which grew 8.4% in the three weeks to October 18, cannot fix a balance sheet with too much debt or too many expensive stores. Administration lets a buyer pick the better stores and leases and leave the rest, which is why several rivals are circling. Higher business rates and wages hit low-priced, labor-heavy retailers hardest. The open question is how many stores and jobs survive a sale.

sources.title: Thousands of jobs at risk with Poundland on brink of administration (ITV)

2026-11-03-12.summary: Poundland filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators on October 29, with AlixPartners lined up for the role. The filing gives about ten working days of protection from creditors while the owner seeks a rescue, and stores remain open. Reports put about 12,000 jobs and roughly 600 UK stores at risk. Owner Gordon Brothers began a sale process in early September, and an earlier rescue bid from Martin Property Group was reportedly rejected. CDS Superstores, Fortress and Modella are reportedly interested in parts of the business. UK retailers also face about £250 million of higher business rates and £2 billion of higher employment costs, according to the British Retail Consortium.
